paragraphs: The Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company," "we," "us," "our" or "the holding company") is a Delaware financial holding company and our primary, wholly-owned subsidiary is The Bancorp Bank, National Association (the "Bank"). The Bank is a federally chartered commercial bank located in Sioux Falls, South Dakota and is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") insured institution. The vast majority of our revenue and income is generated through the Bank. As described more fully below, our business strategy is focused on Fintech Solutions, including program sponsorship, payment services, and sponsored lending. We expect our fintech business to generate non-interest income and attract stable, lower cost deposits which we then seek to deploy into lower risk assets in specialized markets through the specialty lending activities of our Credit Solutions business.
An overview of our operations follows, including discussion of Fintech Solutions, Credit Solutions, and Other Operations.

We are a leading fintech bank, focused on partnering with fintech innovators and providing a dynamic portfolio of payment and lending solutions. Our focus is on continually evolving our product offerings to meet the needs and goals of different partners, and building a strong foundation of technology and services, while maintaining a focus on strong and effective regulatory compliance.

The Fintech Solutions business line partners with fintech companies and other technology focused payment-based providers (collectively "partners") to deliver payment, deposit, and sponsored lending products that attract stable, lower-cost deposits and generate fee income. Deposits generated through these partner relationships are deployed into loan and lease products offered by both Sponsored Lending and the Credit Solutions business line.

Our fintech services are provided to organizations with a pre-existing customer base, and the products are tailored to support or complement the services provided by these organizations to their customers. We typically provide these services under the name and through the facilities of each partner.

The Fintech Solutions division's capabilities include: the sponsored issuance of deposit accounts and debit, credit, and prepaid cards; sponsored lending products for fintech partners; and payment processing solutions, including acquiring, ACH, and near-and real-time payment services in support of its partners.
An overview of our fintech products is as follows:

Program sponsorship includes debit, credit and prepaid cards that we issue for companies that market directly to end users. The Bank issues the cards, provides access to the card networks, maintains deposits, and is the sponsor bank of record for accounts. Our card-accessed deposit account types are diverse and include consumer and business debit, general purpose reloadable prepaid, pre-tax medical spending benefit, payroll, gift, government, corporate incentive, reward, business payment accounts and others.

Fee income from Prepaid, debit card and related sources was $103.5 million and $97.4 million for 2025 and 2024, respectively. The majority of fees that we earn result from contractual fees paid by our partners, computed on a per transaction basis, and monthly service fees. Additionally, we earn interchange fees paid through settlement networks such as Visa or Mastercard, which are also determined on a per transaction basis.

Payment services delivers real-time, end-to-end payment processing, including automated clearing house ("ACH") and Rapid Funds Transfer products. Our ACH accounts facilitate bill payments and our acquiring accounts provide clearing and settlement services for payments made to merchants which must be settled through networks such as Visa or Mastercard.
Fee income from ACH, card and other payment processing was $21.0 million and $14.6 million for 2025 and 2024, respectively.

Sponsored lending, or Fintech loans, consist of short-term loans originated by the Bank, with the marketing and servicing assistance of our partners. Loans receivable originated under fintech agreements are governed by an agreement with the borrower and may include secured credit cards and unsecured short-term extensions of credit. For the secured credit card program, we recognize a loan receivable and a deposit liability for the cash collateral that secures those accounts. Unsecured fintech loans include payroll advance and other short term-extensions of credit, which are typically repaid within a year of origination. As of December 31, 2025, all fintech loans are covered by credit enhancement agreements as discussed further in Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis—Financial Condition—Total Loan Portfolio—Fintech Programs."

We began originating significant volumes of fintech loans in the fourth quarter of 2024, and this segment of our total loan portfolio has grown significantly in 2025, to $1.10 billion, or 15% of our total loan portfolio as of December 31, 2025, from $454.4 million, or 7% as of December 31, 2024.
The revenue generated through fintech loan agreements is primarily fee revenue, and not interest income. Fintech fees were $16.6 million and $4.8 million for 2025 and 2024, respectively.

Business and Strategy
We cannot assure you that we will be able to accomplish our strategic goals as necessary to meet our financial targets.
New lines of business, and new products and services may result in exposure to new risks and the value and earnings related to existing lines of business are subject to market conditions.
We are dependent upon digital delivery channels for our banking and fintech services, and are subject to the risks associated with those channels.
Potential acquisitions may disrupt our business and dilute stockholder value.
The development and use of artificial intelligence ("AI") presents risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business.
Ineffective liquidity management could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operation.
Regulatory and Compliance
We are subject to and may be affected by extensive government regulation or material changes in the regulatory landscape.
Failure to comply with personal data protection and privacy laws can adversely affect our business.
Our enterprise-wide risk management framework, processes and strategies must be effective.
We will be subject to heightened regulatory requirements and experience adverse business consequences if our total assets exceed $10 billion as of December 31 of any calendar year.
We operate in highly competitive markets, and our partnership marketing strategy has been adopted by other institutions with which we compete.

Periods of weak economic, slow growth, and/or inflationary conditions in the U.S. economy have had, and could have significant adverse effects on our business performance, growth prospects, and operating results.
A prolonged U.S. federal government shutdown or default by the United States on government obligations could harm our results of operations.
Changes in interest rates could reduce our income and asset valuations, and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Fintech Solutions Business
There is a significant concentration of deposits and non-interest income that are sourced through partner relationships in our Fintech Solutions business.
Regulatory and legal requirements applicable to the prepaid and debit card industry are unique and can be subject to frequent change.

Changes in rules or standards set by the payment networks, or changes in debit network fees or products or interchange rates, could adversely affect our business, financial position and results of operations.
The potential for fraud in the card payment industry is significant and could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
If our prepaid and debit card and other deposit accounts generated by third-parties were no longer classified as non-brokered, our FDIC insurance expense might increase.
We face fund transfer and payments-related risks.
Agreements between the Bank and its partners related to marketing and servicing fintech loans may subject the Bank to unique compliance, oversight, and other risks.
Unclaimed funds from deposit accounts or represented by unused value on prepaid cards present compliance and other risks.
Credit Solutions Business
We are subject to lending risks.
The quantitative models we use to manage certain accounting and risk management functions may not be effective, which may cause adverse effects on our results of operations and financial condition.

We are exposed to credit risks specific to the population of real estate bridge loans, including risks related to the real estate collateral value and risks related to the execution of the properties' business plan.
Interruptions or failures in our technology solutions, or those of our third-party service providers, could impact or interrupt our ability to service our customers, clients and partners.

The following risk factors, the information set forth under "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be read carefully in connection with evaluating our business. The risks and uncertainties described below could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations and cash flows in future periods and are not the only risks facing our Company. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently do not view as material may also become materially adverse to our business in future periods or if circumstances change.
Our risk factors are organized into sections, and a summary of the content of the sections is as follows:

Business and Strategy – contains discussion of risks related to our strategic goals, growth, new lines of business, products and services, digital delivery channels, acquisitions, artificial intelligence, and liquidity management.

Regulatory and Compliance—contains discussion of risks related to the impact of government regulation or changes in regulation, personal data protection and privacy law compliance, our enterprise risk-management framework, processes and strategies, and the consequences if our balance sheet grows above $10 billion as of December 31 of any calendar year.

Fintech Solutions Business—contains discussion of concentration of partner relationships, regulatory and legal requirements specific to the industry, the impact of changes in rules or standards or rates of the payment networks, fraud risk, the risk of no longer being classified as non-brokered, fund transfer and payment related risks, risk related to partner agreements, and compliance risk related to unclaimed funds.

Credit Solutions Business—contains discussion of lending risks, model risk, credit fraud and regulatory risks related to partner agreements for marketing and servicing loans, risks specific to real estate bridge lending, and SBA lending program risks.

paragraphs: We remain focused on growing our fintech revenues through new partnerships, products and services. Fintech loans of $1.10 billion as of December 31, 2025 increased 142% compared to the December 31, 2024 balance of $454.4 million. Certain loan fees on fintech loans are recorded as non-interest income, and totaled $16.6 million in 2025 compared to $4.8 million in 2024. In addition, our fees earned from ACH, card and other payment processing and Prepaid, debit card and related revenues also grew to $124.6 million in 2025 from $112.0 million in 2024.

We continue to invest in our infrastructure, with a focus on investing in AI tools to gain efficiency and productivity of our people and platform, and reallocating or reducing resources where appropriate. We believe that our infrastructure can accommodate significant additional growth without proportionate increases in expense. In addition, as part of our strategies we will reallocate or reduce resources where appropriate. As part of those efforts, in the fourth quarter of 2025 we restructured our institutional banking business to de-emphasize growth and reallocate space on our balance sheet. This action resulted in a $1.1 million restructuring charge in the fourth quarter of 2025 and $8.0 million in run-rate expense reductions beginning in early 2026.

For 2025, the full year capital return was $375.0 million, and we repurchased 5.646 million shares, or 12% of issued and outstanding shares, at an average price of $66.42. We began returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases in 2021, and for the past five years of repurchases from 2021 through 2025 we have returned $825.0 million in total, repurchasing 18.998 million shares, or 33% of shares outstanding from December 31, 2020. Since 2021, we have returned 94% of our net income through share repurchases.
Our 2026 share repurchase plan was approved by our Board of Directors on July 7, 2025, and includes authorization for up to $200 million of repurchases.

paragraphs: The Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company," "we," "us," "our" or "the holding company") 為一間位於德國的財務控股公司，我們的主要、完全擁有子公司為 The Bancorp Bank, National Association (the "Bank"). The Bank 為一間位於南達科他州蘇城的聯邦特許商業銀行，並為美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）所 insure 的機構。我們絕大多數的營業收入與所得皆來自 The Bank。如後文更詳細說明，我們的業務策略聚焦於 Fintech 解決方案，包括 programme sponsorship、支付服務及 sponsored lending。我們預期 fintech 事業能產生非利息收入，並吸引穩定、成本較低的存款，我們隨後將這些存款運用於專門市場中較低風險的資產，透過 Credit Solutions 事業的專門貸款活動。
以下為我們營運的概覽，包括對 Fintech 解決方案、Credit Solutions 以及其他營運的討論。
我們為一間領先的 fintech 銀行，專注於與 fintech 創新者合作，並提供多元的支付與貸款解決方案。我們的重點在於持續進化產品組合，以符合不同合作夥伴的需要與目標，並建立強固的科技與服務基礎，同時維持對強而有效的監管合規的關注。
Fintech 解決方案業務線與 fintech 公司及其他以科技為導向的支付型服務提供者（合稱 "partners"）合作，以提供支付、存款及 sponsored lending 產品，以吸引穩定、成本較低的存款，並產生手續費收入。透過這些合作夥伴關係所產生的存款，會被運用於 Sponsored Lending 及 Credit Solutions 事業線所提供的貸款與租賃產品。
我們的 fintech 服務提供給已有現有客戶羣的組織，產品則根據這些組織對其客戶所提供的服務進行調整或補充。我們通常在合作夥伴的名義下，透過其設施提供這些服務。
Fintech 解決方案部門的業務能力包括：為公司發行存款帳戶及 debit、credit 與 prepaid 卡的 sponsored 發行；為 fintech 合作夥伴提供的 sponsored lending 產品；以及支付處理解決方案，包括 acquiring、ACH 及近實時支付服務，以支援其合作夥伴。
以下為我們 fintech 產品的概覽：

Program sponsorship 包含我們為直接對最終用戶進行市場行銷的公司發行的 debit、credit 與 prepaid 卡。The Bank 發行這些卡，提供對卡網路的存取權，管理存款，並為帳戶的正式發起銀行。我們的卡存取存款帳戶種類多元，包括消費者與企業 debit、一般用途可重複充值 prepaid、預扣醫療支出福利、薪資、禮品、政府、企業激勵、獎勵、企業付款帳戶及其他類型。
預付卡、信用卡及相關來源的費用收入為 103.5 百萬美元及 97.4 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年及 2024 年。我們所賺取的費用大多來自於合作夥伴依據契約支付的費用，按每筆交易計算，並包含每月服務費用。此外，我們亦透過 Visa 或 Mastercard 等結算網路收取交換費用，亦為按每筆交易計算。
支付服務提供即時、端到端的支付處理服務，包括自動清算所（"ACH"）及 Rapid Funds Transfer 產品。我們的 ACH 帳戶用於帳單支付，而我們的 acquiring 帳戶則為商家提供支付結清與結算服務，這些支付必須透過 Visa 或 Mastercard 等網路進行結清與結算。
ACH、信用卡及其他支付處理的費用收入為 2025 年 21.0 百萬美元及 2024 年 14.6 百萬美元。

 sponsored lending，或稱為 Fintech 貸款，是由銀行發放的短期貸款，並由我們的委外夥伴協助行銷與服務。根據 fintech 協議發放的貸款應收帳款，由借款人與我們之間的協議所規範，可能包含擔保信用卡及無擔保的短期信貸延長。對於擔保信用卡計畫，我們會確認貸款應收帳款及存款負債，以擔保這些帳戶的現金擔保品。無擔保的 fintech 貸款包含薪資預支及其他短期信貸延長，通常在發放後一年內償還。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，所有 fintech 貸款均受信用增強協議保障，如後述 Item 7，"管理層討論與分析—財務狀況—總貸款組合—Fintech 程式" 所述。
我們於 2024 年第四季開始發放大量 fintech 貸款，且我們總貸款組閤中此部分已顯著成長，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，總貸款組閤中 fintech 貸款為 1,100,000,000 美元，佔總貸款組合 15%，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 454.4 百萬美元，佔總貸款組合 7% 相較。
透過 fintech 貸款協議產生的收入主要為費用收入，而非利息收入。fintech 費用為 2025 年 16.6 百萬美元及 2024 年 4.8 百萬美元。

paragraphs: 我們持續著力於透過新合作夥伴、產品與服務來成長我們的金融科技收入。截至2025年12月31日，金融科技貸款為1.10十億美元，較2024年12月31日的454.4百萬美元增加142%。部分金融科技貸款的貸款費用被記入非利息收入，2025年總計為16.6百萬美元，較2024年的4.8百萬美元增加。此外，我們從ACH、卡及其它付款處理以及預付、提款卡及相關收入所賺取的費用也成長至2025年的124.6百萬美元，較2024年的112.0百萬美元增加。

我們持續投資於我們的基礎建設，重點在於投資AI工具以提高我們人員與平台的效率與生產力，並在適當的情況下重新配置或減少資源。我們認為，我們的基礎建設可以容納顯著的成長，而不需要相同比例的費用增加。此外，作為我們策略的一部分，我們將在適當的情況下重新配置或減少資源。作為這些努力的一部分，我們在2025年第四季重新結構我們的機構銀行業務，以降低成長的強調並重新配置我們資產負債表上的空間。此舉導致2025年第四季產生1.1百萬美元的重組費用，並自2026年初起產生8.0百萬美元的運營費用減少。
2025年全年資本回報為375.0百萬美元，我們以平均價格66.42美元購回5.646百萬股，即發行在外股數的12%。我們自2021年起開始透過股票購回回饋資本給股東，從2021年至2025年這五年的股票購回總計為825.0百萬美元，購回18.998百萬股，即2020年12月31日發行在外股數的33%。自2021年起，我們透過股票購回回饋了94%的淨收入。
我們2026年的股票購回計畫已於2025年7月7日經董事會批准，並授權最多200百萬美元的購回金額。

headings: 競爭—包含對我們所從事競爭市場的討論。
經濟—包含對負面經濟環境時期、美國聯邦政府停擺及利率變動對我們業務影響的討論。
營運—包含對科技中斷或故障風險、網路安全風險、第三方委外風險及關鍵員工風險的討論。
稅務與會計—包含對會計估計風險、會計政策或標準變更風險及內部控制風險的討論。
業務與策略
我們無法保證我們將能實現必要的戰略目標以達成財務目標。
新業務線及新產品與服務可能導致面臨新風險，且現有業務線的價值與獲利表現將受市場條件影響。
我們依賴數位交付渠道提供銀行及金融科技服務，並面臨與這些渠道相關的風險。
潛在的併購可能幹擾我們的業務並稀釋股東價值。
人工智慧（"AI"）的發展與應用帶來風險與挑戰，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
流動性管理不當可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
法規與合規
我們受制於廣泛的政府法規，並可能受重大法規變動的影響。
未能遵守個人資料保護與隱私權法規可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們的企業風險管理架構、流程與策略必須有效。
若我們的總資產在任何會計年度的12月31日達到10十億美元以上，我們將面臨更嚴格的法規要求，並可能遭遇不利的業務後果。
我們經營於高度競爭的市場，且我們的夥伴行銷策略已被我們競爭對手的機構所採用。
美國經濟在弱勢經濟、成長緩慢及/或通貨膨脹條件期間，已對我們的業務表現、成長前景及營運結果產生，並可能產生重大不利影響。
美國聯邦政府長時間停擺或美國對政府義務的違約，可能對我們的營運結果造成損害。
利率的變動可能降低我們的收入與資產評價，並對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
金融科技解決方案業務
我們的金融科技解決方案業務中，有相當程度的存款及非利息收入來自於夥伴關係。
預付卡及提款卡產業所適用的監管及法律要求具有獨特性，且可能經常變動。
支付網路所設立的規則或標準變動，或提款網路費用、產品或交換率變動，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
信用卡支付產業中詐欺的潛在風險相當高，可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
若本公司由第三方所產生的預付卡及提款卡與其他存款帳戶不再被歸類為非經紀類帳戶，我們的FDIC保險費用可能會增加。
我們面臨資金轉移及付款相關的風險。
銀行與其合作夥伴之間關於行銷及服務金融科技貸款的協議，可能使銀行面臨獨特的合規、監督及其他風險。
存款帳戶中的未領款資金或預付卡上未使用的價值，可能帶來合規及其他風險。
信貸解決方案業務
我們面臨貸款風險。
我們用來管理某些會計及風險管理功能的量化模型，可能無法有效運作，這可能會對我們的營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司面臨與不動產過橋貸款羣體相關的信用風險，包括與不動產擔保價值相關的風險，以及與不動產資產營運計畫執行相關的風險。
我們的科技解決方案或第三方服務供應商的中斷或失敗，可能影響或中斷我們為客戶、客戶及合作夥伴提供服務的能力。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及風險。下列風險因素、資訊申明部分所載的「風險因素與未來展望聲明」以及本年度報告表10-K所載的其他資訊，應仔細閱讀以評估本公司業務。下列所述的風險與不確定性可能對本公司未來期間的業務、財務狀況與營運成果及現金流產生重大且不利的影響，並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。此外，尚有其他未被本公司知悉或目前未被視為重要的風險與不確定性，可能在未來期間對本公司業務產生重大不利影響，或因情勢改變而變得重要。
本公司風險因素分為各節，各節內容摘要如下：
業務與策略 – 包含與本公司戰略目標、成長、新業務線、產品與服務、數位通路、併購、人工智慧及流動性管理相關的風險討論。
法規與合規—包含有關政府法規或法規變更影響、個人資料保護與隱私權法規遵循、企業風險管理架構、流程與策略，以及若本公司資產負債表在任何會計年度12月31日資產規模超過10十億美元所產生後果之風險討論。
金融科技解決方案業務 – 包含與合作夥伴關係集中度、產業特定的法規與法律要求、支付網路規則或標準或利率變動的影響、詐欺風險、不再被歸類為非經紀商的風險、資金轉移與支付相關風險、合作夥伴契約相關風險，以及未申領資金相關的合規風險的討論。
信貸解決方案業務 – 包含貸款風險、模型風險、信貸詐欺與與合作夥伴契約相關的行銷與貸款服務的法規風險、與不動產過橋貸款相關的特定風險，以及小企業管理局貸款計畫的風險討論。
